title: Interoperability conductor: translate third-party chat request/response shape to Redwood streaming + tool protocol
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Implement a protocol translation layer ('conductor') that accepts widely-used third-party chat API request/response shapes and maps them to Redwood's unified streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured-output runtime.

Goal: let customers proxy existing integrations (SDKs, webhooks, legacy agents) with minimal changes while preserving Redwood SLOs, structured output enforcement, and telemetry. The conductor must support: incremental token streaming deltas, function/tool call negotiation and handoff, explicit structured JSON outputs with schema validation, role/metadata mapping, idempotency, and clear error and rate-limit semantics.

Out-of-scope for initial iteration: full upstream SDK emulation (we only implement the subset used by top 5 customers), multi-tenant per-connection backpressure shaping (follow-on), and language-specific SDK shims.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming third-party chat format can be proxied to Redwood core with <=5% median latency overhead under a 100 req/s baseline
Streaming deltas map 1:1 to Redwood stream frames such that client receives coherent partial tool_call signals (start/args/end) without JSON corruption
Function/tool invocation semantics: remote function_call requests are surfaced as Redwood tool invocation events and return tool outputs mapped back into the third-party response shape
Structured outputs validated against supplied JSON schema; validation failures return clear, mapped error payloads to client
Telemetry: each proxied request emits correlation_id, original_request_shape, mapped_model_variant, and risk flags into tracing system
design_decisions: Wire format: adopt Redwood's chunked streaming envelope as canonical; translator emits compatibility frames for clients that expect event-stream/lines-based payloads
Function calls: canonicalize to Redwood tool RPC model (tool_id, args, status) to simplify retry/timeout semantics across backends
Streaming strategy: prefer continuous delta stream with reassembly guidance in translator; avoid batched replays to minimize tail-latency impact
Schema enforcement: perform soft validation (warning) in alpha build, hard validation (reject) gated behind feature flag after a one-week dogfood period
Fallbacks: if client requests an unavailable feature (e.g., shared conversation state), return a mapped 422 with 'feature_not_supported' and an instrumentation counter
tradeoffs_and_risks: Completeness vs latency: rich compatibility (mapping every optional field) increases code surface and test matrix; we limit initial shape coverage to high-frequency fields to reduce regression risk
Security: accepting arbitrary tool arguments introduces injection risks; we will strip unrecognized metadata and require KMS-enforced tool permissions for enterprise deployments
Operational complexity: two-layer mapping (external->canonical->runtime) adds more places for telemetry loss; invest in end-to-end correlation ids early
Backpressure: proxy must avoid unbounded buffering of streaming tool outputs; we'll implement a per-connection buffer cap and backpressure signals to upstream clients
implementation_notes: Create 'interop-conductor' microservice behind existing API gateway and route via new /v1/compat chat endpoint
Translator components: message-normalizer, streaming-recomposer, tool-call-bridge, schema-validator, error-mapper
Idempotency: map external request idempotency keys to Redwood request tokens and persist short-lived mapping in Redis (TTL 60s)
Telemetry: add span 'interop.translate' with attributes: external_proto, mapped_fields, delta_frames_count
Testing: unit harness for delta streaming reassembly, e2e harness that simulates partial function_call streaming and tool timeouts
open_questions: How should streaming aborts initiated by the inbound client be preferred: signal runtime cancel or let tool run to completion? (technical leads leaning toward cancel with best-effort tool-side rollback)
Do we need to preserve original field order on message arrays for downstream clients that assert positional semantics? (we will preserve order for the initial set of roles: system/user/assistant)

Do we transcode client-supplied function schemas into Redwood's tool descriptor model on the fly or require pre-registered tool descriptors? (opt for dynamic one-off mapping for alpha, require registration for GA)
What level of response fidelity is acceptable for cost-conscious tiers (trim streaming metadata vs full fidelity)? (policy required from PM)
Edge case: partial JSON emitted across multiple streaming deltas — how to best surface parsing errors to the original client? (translator must buffer until schema-complete then validate)
Operational: throttle policy when translator sees >2x baseline fanout to downstream runtime; should we shed with 429 or queue?
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype translator skeleton + simple pass-through for non-streaming requests; add correlation IDs (OWN: Daniel)
Week 2: implement streaming-recomposer and delta tests, validate against sample payloads from top 5 customers (OWN: Sofia Ramirez + Daniel)
Week 3: tool-call-bridge PoC integrating with sandboxed tool runner; verify argument streaming and partial outputs (OWN: Alex Chen)
Week 4: schema validator + feature-flagged hard validation; dogfood internally and run traffic replay tests (OWN: Maya Patel)
Week 5: run security review, finalize error-mapping, and ship alpha behind account toggle (OWN: Priya Narang)
Post-alpha: collect telemetry, iterate on missing fields, formalize registration flow for GA
